name: Jeremy Todd
current_role: Salesperson and Libertarian Party of Kentucky activist
bio: Jeremy Todd is a Northern Kentucky resident and the Libertarian Party nominee for Kentucky's 4th congressional district. His campaign biography says he grew up in the South and has led business teams of up to 300 people. The party nominated him in May 2026 after Rep. Thomas Massie lost the Republican primary, and he qualified for the ballot with more than 750 signatures.

platform.point: Calls affordability his top priority and blames money printing and national debt; wants spending cuts across the board and debt reduction.
Wants income taxes cut and eventually eliminated, and supports ending the Federal Reserve's control of the currency.
Wants to bring troops home, end ongoing foreign interventions, oppose any return of the draft and keep a defense-only military.
Backs a plain reading of the Second Amendment and opposes gun-free zones and added regulations on lawful gun owners.
Opposes any government censorship effort and government coordination with companies or media to shape public opinion.
Describes himself as a pro-life Libertarian who wants abortion policy left to the states and no federal funding for abortion providers.
Opposes open borders and supports secure, enforced borders alongside a clear and fair legal immigration process.
Supports the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship rule for voter registration and opposes foreign-linked lobbying influence, including AIPAC.

economy.evidence: His site calls for a sharp cut in taxes across the board and for ending the Federal Reserve.

welfare.evidence: He calls for spending cuts across the board and says the answer to high costs is less socialism, not more.

liberty.evidence: Averages his opposition to gun restrictions and to government censorship with his pro-life stance that leaves abortion to the states.

immigration.evidence: He opposes open borders and wants secure, enforced borders while keeping a fair legal immigration process, a general balanced statement.

foreign.evidence: He pledges to end what he calls the permanent war state, bring troops home and cut back military action abroad.

notes: Positions come from the issue pages on jeremy-todd.com; ballot access details come from LINK nky coverage (https://linknky.com/news/2026/06/02/libertarian-ballot-access-kentucky-4th-congressional-district/). No statements were found on surveillance, energy, tech, education or religion in public life.

name: Gerardo Serrano
current_role: Farmer and civil asset forfeiture activist
bio: Gerardo Serrano is a farmer from Tyner, Kentucky, running as an independent for Kentucky's 5th congressional district. He became known after Customs and Border Protection seized his pickup truck in 2015 over five bullets found in it, and he has since campaigned against civil asset forfeiture. He previously ran in Republican primaries for the 5th District, including a 2022 loss to Rep. Hal Rogers.

platform.point: Says his candidacy grows out of fighting civil asset forfeiture and defending due process after the government seized his truck.
Favors a fair tax or replacing the income tax with tariffs on imported goods.
Wants the government to get out of the way, remove regulations that slow growth, and shrink its size.
Wants the US to stay out of wars Congress has not approved and to leave current unauthorized wars.
Supports free and open health insurance markets with fewer federal and state rules.
Open to raising the benefit age and letting very wealthy people pay in without drawing benefits.
Strongly supports a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution.

economy.evidence: In his iVoterGuide questionnaire (answered for a 2018 race) he backs ending the income tax, a fair tax and cutting regulations.

welfare.evidence: In the same questionnaire he strongly disagreed that government must ensure everyone has a livable income or health insurance.

liberty.evidence: Averages his opposition to abortion except to save the mother's life and his opposition to more gun control with mixed LGBTQ answers (one-man-one-woman marriage, but restroom use by gender identity).

security.evidence: He says his campaign centers on fighting civil asset forfeiture and government intrusion on due process and the Bill of Rights.

immigration.evidence: He agreed with building a border wall and infrastructure for complete control of entry, and was neutral on sanctuary cities.

foreign.evidence: He calls for a non-aggression foreign policy and leaving wars not approved by Congress, while also agreeing that a strong military keeps the peace.

notes: Positions come from his own iVoterGuide questionnaire answers, which the guide shows under a 2018 race, and the page also lists his 2026 candidacy; serranoforcongress.org did not resolve. His answers on religion were mixed and nothing was found on energy, tech or education, so those stay null.

name: Lisa Ballay
current_role: Senior Director of Surgical Services (healthcare executive)
bio: Lisa Ballay is a New Orleans healthcare executive and former frontline nurse with more than 25 years in healthcare, and she is the Libertarian candidate in Louisiana's 2nd District. She is president of the West Jefferson Hospital Foundation and was appointed to a New Orleans neighborhood housing advisory committee in 2017 and to the Louisiana State Museum Board in 2025.

platform.point: Her first legislative priority is healthcare price transparency, more competition and less administrative burden.
Calls for federal fiscal discipline, removing regulations that raise business costs, and more competition in insurance markets.
Supports no federal tax on tips, overtime or basic necessities, and a tax code short enough to fit on one page.
Opposes shifting Medicaid costs onto patients and wants SNAP kept as a safety net, with better paths to work.
Wants Louisiana to keep its share of federal offshore energy revenue and spend it on coastal restoration and flood protection.
Supports clear country-of-origin labels and the same safety inspections for imported seafood that Louisiana shrimpers meet.
Supports border security and immigration enforcement, but wants it constitutional, targeted and overseen, including audits of detention contractors.
Highlights $186 billion in improper federal payments and says Washington must track where its money goes without cutting care.

economy.evidence: She backs cutting regulations that raise business costs, no tax on tips, overtime or necessities, and a one-page tax code, plus stricter import seafood rules.

welfare.evidence: She would protect Medicaid and SNAP from cuts but favors market competition in healthcare and stronger paths to work for able adults.

security.evidence: She says federal agents operating in communities must respect due process, clear standards and oversight, a general statement.

immigration.evidence: She supports securing the border and enforcing immigration law, but only in a constitutional, targeted and accountable way, and wants lawful immigration reformed.

energy.evidence: Her platform says Louisiana should be one of the cheapest places to power a home and backs domestic energy, a general statement.

notes: The first-round description of her as a digital creator appears to have come from lisaballay.com, which belongs to a different person, so the role was corrected using her campaign site ballayforcongress.com and its questionnaire page. No positions were found on social issues, foreign policy, tech, education or religion.

name: Sam Husseini
current_role: Communications director, Institute for Public Accuracy
bio: Sam Husseini has been communications director of the Institute for Public Accuracy since 1997 and previously worked at Fairness and Accuracy in Reporting and the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee. He studied applied math and logic at Carnegie Mellon University and has lived in Maryland's 4th District for more than 20 years. The Maryland Green Party nominated him for the 4th District in 2026, and he formally launched his campaign in August.

platform.point: Supports an enhanced Medicare for All system and opposes privatizing Medicare and Medicaid or weakening Social Security.
Opposes the proposed $1.5 trillion military budget and US strikes on Iran, Yemen and Venezuela, and argues peace means affordability.
Wants US funding for Israel's war in Gaza stopped and runs against AIPAC's influence on the district's elections.
Calls for higher taxes on the very wealthy, ending corporate welfare and regulation to bring down housing, food and childcare costs.
Pledges to abolish ICE and criticizes its detention and surveillance practices as human rights violations.
Wants to confront big tech companies and data centers over their effects on society, the economy and the environment.
Supports banning individual stock trading by members of Congress.
Backs publicly owned open-source voting, a national elections commission, public campaign financing and fewer barriers for third parties.

economy.evidence: His issues page calls for taxing oligarchs more, ending corporate welfare and using regulation to address affordability.

welfare.evidence: He supports enhanced Medicare for All covering everyone and opposes privatizing Medicare and Medicaid.

liberty.evidence: Based only on speech: he opposes what he calls attacks on free speech and the right to protest.

security.evidence: He pledges to protect civil liberties, criticizes post-9/11 security structures, big tech surveillance and police militarization, and would abolish ICE.

immigration.evidence: He pledges to stop and abolish ICE and calls current detention practices human rights violations.

foreign.evidence: He opposes US wars on Iran, Yemen and Venezuela, US funding for Israel's war in Gaza, and the $1.5 trillion military budget.

tech.evidence: He says he will take on big tech and data centers over their harms, a general statement without a named bill.

notes: Sources are samhusseini.com (home, about and issues pages) and his campaign posts at husseini.substack.com. No specific positions were found on energy or climate policy, education, abortion, guns or religion.

name: Arnett Satterla
bio: Arnett Satterla is the Libertarian Party nominee for Michigan's 1st congressional district, and the Libertarian Party of Michigan lists him among its 2026 candidates. No campaign biography was found.
notes: Checked the Libertarian Party of Michigan's 2026 candidate page (photo card only), the iVoterGuide MI-1 race page (no answers), web searches and likely campaign domains; the Michigan Advance guide was blocked. No campaign site, social account or stated positions were found.

name: LaVeta Davenport
bio: LaVeta Davenport is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 1st Congressional District in 2026. She is the founder of Levadeh, a Detroit-based nonprofit started in 2021 that offers mostly free educational resources focused on health, education, relationships and ownership.
notes: Checked the iVoterGuide MI-1 race page (which links her Facebook and levadeh.org), the Levadeh site, the Green Party of Michigan site (only outdated candidate pages) and web searches; the Michigan Advance guide was blocked. No campaign site or issue statements were found.

name: Doc Kovaly
current_role: Retired postal worker and anti-abortion activist
bio: Robert "Doc" Kovaly is the U.S. Taxpayers Party nominee for Michigan's 1st Congressional District in 2026 and is listed as a retired postal worker. His campaign site presents him as a longtime anti-abortion activist who has been arrested during protests, and its campaign centers on television ads opposing abortion.

platform.point: His campaign centers on ending abortion and opposing late-term abortion in Michigan, and runs TV ads opposing abortion.

liberty.evidence: Based only on abortion: his campaign site is devoted to ending abortion, including opposition to late-term abortion.

notes: Found his campaign site doc.vote, which covers only abortion, and a Facebook link on iVoterGuide's MI-1 page; the U.S. Taxpayers Party of Michigan site did not resolve and the Michigan Advance guide was blocked. No statements were found on any topic other than abortion.

name: Liz Hakola
bio: Liz Hakola is the Working Class Party nominee for Michigan's 1st Congressional District in 2026, after also running for the seat in 2022 and 2024. She retired after 31 years as a manager at Michigan Consolidated Gas, lives in Baraga County, and ran for Baraga city council in 2020. She has given voter-education talks for the League of Women Voters in the Copper Country.

platform.point: In her 2020 city council race she backed universal broadband and better cell service to attract businesses and young workers.
In 2020 she said she wanted to protect voting rights and open government to as many people and ideas as possible.

notes: Checked Working Class Party posts (which list her but have no written statements from her), 2024 race coverage (the Alpena News reported she did not respond to interview requests), a 2020 Mining Gazette profile and the iVoterGuide MI-1 page. No 2026 statements on the ten topics were found, and the party's shared program was not used to score her.
